headline: Medium prompt-injection and data-leakage risks from Haystack MCP/REST ingestion paired with a leak-oriented audio-speech agent; no direct evidence of shared runtime, so interaction risk is inferred.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Haystack exposes MCP servers and REST APIs, so it can ingest external content by default; if system_prompts_leaks feeds or relays attacker-controlled text, Haystack may treat it as instructions. The pair lacks documented provenance controls, so the interaction is inferred rather than directly evidenced.
conditions: IF agent_b forwards untrusted text into agent_a via MCP or REST
IF agent_a parses retrieved content as instructions without provenance tagging
mitigations: Disable MCP endpoints not needed for the workflow
Add a strict instruction/data delimiter in the Haystack prompt template
Require provenance labels on all retrieved text
Route agent_b outputs through a human review step before ingestion
requires-engineering: implement content-sanitization and provenance enforcement

B_data_leakage.rationale: Haystack has broad network egress, but the only touched data class listed is anonymous usage statistics, and system_prompts_leaks shows no data classes touched and no network egress. With no shared workspace or sensitive data documented, leakage risk is limited and mostly configuration-dependent.
conditions: IF both agents are placed in a shared workspace containing sensitive files
IF agent_a is configured to ingest those files and transmit them over network egress
mitigations: Keep the agents in separate workspaces
Do not mount sensitive directories into Haystack
Restrict Haystack egress to approved domains
Verify agent_b remains offline-only
requires-engineering: add OS-level sandboxing and network allowlists

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Haystack can call REST APIs and MCP servers, while system_prompts_leaks has no write or network capabilities documented. There is no evidence of overlapping mutable-resource writes, so direct capability conflict is unlikely; uncertainty stays low because the pairwise orchestration is undocumented.
conditions: IF both agents are granted write access to the same filesystem or database
IF an orchestrator maps both to the same mutable OAuth scope
mitigations: Avoid shared writable directories
Separate credentials per agent
Disable unnecessary API write methods
Check orchestrator locking before concurrent runs
requires-engineering: add resource locks for shared mutable targets

D_cascading_error.rationale: Haystack is a search-RAG agent, so its outputs are likely to be consumed downstream; if system_prompts_leaks treats those outputs as authoritative, errors or fabricated retrievals can cascade into user-visible actions. No verification pipeline is documented, so the safer medium severity is chosen over low.
conditions: IF agent_b consumes Haystack output without independent verification
IF Haystack retrieval errors are rendered or acted on downstream
mitigations: Insert a verification step before downstream use
Require citations for every retrieved claim
Flag low-confidence retrievals for review
Limit agent_b to summarization rather than action-taking
requires-engineering: add automated fact-checking gates

E_compliance.rationale: No residency, certification, retention, or subject-rights mismatch is documented for either agent. Haystack only lists anonymous usage statistics, and system_prompts_leaks lists no data classes touched, so a compliance breach pathway is not evidenced in the profiles.
conditions: IF future documentation shows regulated data classes flowing through either agent
IF a residency or retention policy mismatch is introduced
mitigations: Document data-class handling for both agents
Record residency and retention policies
Review compliance obligations before deployment
